learner_operation: Evaluate dy/dx=f(x,y) at three isolated points and identify the diagram with those segment slopes. Necessary operation: substitute each coordinate pair into the displayed f and match the resulting local slopes; coordinate roles, coefficient signs and diagram answer positions are incidental assignments.

fixed_features.feature: Three isolated points, one radio answer and five image choices
fixed_features.justification: Seven source exercises use the same three-substitution workload and complete five-image response bank; e-8505 explains drawing local segments.

fixed_features.feature: Finite, defined slopes with equal-scale axes
fixed_features.justification: A segment must represent f(x,y); denominators cannot vanish at assessed points. Equal scaling preserves slope geometry.

fixed_features.feature: One reversed-correct diagram plus the same three formula-based distractors in every default bank
fixed_features.justification: Author claims method-based distractors. Each alone can be plausible, but fixing their combined relationship to correctness lacks a source or instructional necessity and causes the demonstrated defect.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Any displayed position can hold the unique mathematically matching geometry. Shuffle distractors and change eligible distractor constructions without introducing new prerequisites.
answer_roles.observed: Positions vary, but default correct geometry is always assigned a reversed clone; other formulas tend to agree in direction with the correct clone.

answer_roles.role: Signs, zeros and magnitudes attached to coordinates
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Change coefficients, signs or selected coordinates and derive all dependent content. No point, sign pattern, zero count or term is instructionally required to remain qualifying.
answer_roles.observed: Six forms, signed point/parameter variation and changing sign/zero counts observed. Relevant counterfactuals update correct diagrams, explanations and native grading.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Wrong diagrams can contain varied local substitution or sign errors, preserving one correct five-image bank and visible distinctions. There is no requirement that only the correct diagram have a full reflected clone.
answer_roles.observed: Recognizable systematic bank construction creates an equation-free predictor in all six tested template subgroups.

coverage.case: All seven complete observed banks and canonical example
coverage.result: Seven source prompts exact; all 35 original image geometries match generated bank geometries within 1.1 degrees of independent raster extraction; full banks compared as multisets, not captured array order. Canonical slopes 1,-1,0 reproduced. Two missing stored keys/solutions are documented inferences, not claimed source fields.

counterfactuals.change: With rational-square points fixed, change coefficient a from 1 to -1 (seed 73661).
counterfactuals.expected: Reverse all three slopes, alter the displayed equation, correct diagram and substitutions; the prior correct diagram becomes a wrong choice.
counterfactuals.observed: Slopes [-1/2,4,1/3] become [1/2,-4,-1/3]. Actual screenshots 015/016 show the change, and the native grader rejects the prior geometry and accepts the new correct choice.
counterfactuals.justification: Substitution depends on the signed coefficient; e-8505 and tutorial 5050 explain deriving each segment from the right-hand side.

counterfactuals.change: Hold f=y^2/x fixed and replace point (1,2) with (2,2).
counterfactuals.expected: Only that target center and slope change, from 4 to 2; other slopes and substitutions are preserved.
counterfactuals.observed: Correct image moves the center to (2,2), draws slope 2, and solution shows 4/2=2. Native grader accepts that geometry. Screenshots 015/018 inspected.
counterfactuals.justification: The source operation explicitly substitutes coordinates; targets are eligible answer-bearing inputs.

counterfactuals.change: Reverse presentation order of the three points while keeping their coordinate values and equation fixed.
counterfactuals.expected: Preserve the correct coordinate-to-slope diagram, while reordering the substitution exposition.
counterfactuals.observed: Prompt and correct PNG SHA256 are unchanged, coordinate-slope maps identical; native grader accepts the same mathematical image. Solution rows reorder consistently. Screenshots 015/017 inspected.
counterfactuals.justification: e-8505 derives independent local segments; listing order does not affect any f(x,y).

shortcut_probes.cue: A unique pair of diagrams has every segment slope reflected; choose its member with the most nonzero segment-direction matches to the other three diagrams.
shortcut_probes.subgroup: constant_product authored bank, unique mirror pair and unequal direction scores
shortcut_probes.strategy: Ignore the differential equation, its coefficients, and substitutions. Compare reflected line shapes and signs across choices; score agreement with the remaining three diagrams. Abstain on ties.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: 5/6 decisive predictions correct; baseline is uniform guessing among five choices (0.2), conditional on the same visible unique-pair/unequal-score subgroup. The cue uses only relationships between answer diagrams; it does not compute f at any point. This is incidental even though sign tests using the equation would be legitimate. Finite, deliberately bounded test, not a population estimate.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Select the higher-consensus member of the unique pointwise-reflected image pair, ignoring the equation.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Five of five delivered runner predictions are correct, versus 0.2 uniform-guess baseline. All five submissions were accepted by the actual native grader. Choice UUIDs, labels, position and filename strings are not used by the strategy.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Always select the first displayed image.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: 6/36 successes; uniform guessing among five choices is 0.2. Position shuffling avoids a fixed first-answer shortcut, but it leaves the diagram-relationship shortcut intact.

stages_examined: Generator rejection/resampling at fresh explicit seeds: 53 attempted parameter sets, 17 resampled for visual bank indistinguishability, 36 final records.
Requested easy difficulty, normalization, stable identities and captured-inventory/within-batch deduplication through actual shared prepare_records.
Learner fresh/usable eligibility and difficulty-first deterministic weighted selection rule inspected; read-only captured-inventory plus hypothetical accepted-record fixtures.
delivery.result: 36/36 independent and 5/5 runner records survive filtering. Equation-free cue remains 31/32 decisive independent predictions and 5/5 runner predictions; native grader accepts all 36 correct predictions and rejects the sole wrong prediction. Captured basis 5125 contains 10 generated moderate/hard instances with the same cue. Selection rules do not inspect bank geometry: fresh easy affected records remain reachable. No publication preparation file exists; shared read-only filtering was used.

limitations: Audit supports a demonstrated structural shortcut, not absence of all shortcuts or a population success estimate. Only six fresh records per source equation form were needed to demonstrate the gap; no quota inference.
Two original questions lack captured correct links/solutions; their mathematics is inferred from complete image banks.

Inventory is captured at basis 5125 and can change. Exact affected UUID/entity IDs are in affected-inventory.json. Full 17-bank inspection distinguishes a lack of the tested cue in source banks from future behavior.

Live learner weights/history, usable-entity runtime checks and future assigned DB IDs were not supplied. Selection fixture results are conditional reachability checks, not a prediction of a live learner sequence.

Only requested easy generation is certified for scope; source replay includes seven exercise profiles. Moderate/hard stored questions were examined for the demonstrated cue, not certified as newly generated difficulty bands.
